External links for this lesson. Every link below was checked with `curl` on 2026-11-13 (HTTP 200) and the page title confirmed. The regulation text quoted in the lesson comes from this repo's `sources/` copies (eCFR Versioner API); the Cornell links are verified-loading mirrors for checking current text. The CDC CLIA page returned 403 to an automated request, so it is not linked.

- **[Cornell LII: 42 CFR 493.2, Definitions](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/42/493.2)** — the "laboratory" definition that CMS says decides CLIA applicability, plus "certificate of accreditation" and "equivalency." Use it to check the current wording. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-13 (HTTP 200).
- **[Cornell LII: 42 CFR 493.3, Applicability](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/42/493.3)** — the basic rule and the three exceptions. Use it when someone asks whether a facility is outside CLIA. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-13 (HTTP 200).
- **[Cornell LII: 42 CFR 493.61, Requirements for a certificate of accreditation](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/42/493.61)** — what a lab holding Lakeshore's certificate type must do, including treating PT samples like patient samples. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-13 (HTTP 200).
- **[Cornell LII: 42 CFR Part 493, Laboratory Requirements](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/42/part-493)** — the whole part, for browsing ahead to the sections modules 2 to 5 use. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-13 (HTTP 200).
- **[Cornell LII: 21 CFR 610.40, Test requirements](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/610.40)** — FDA's donor testing rule, including paragraph (f), which ties required testing to CLIA certification. The copy in `sources/` is a dated snapshot. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-13 (HTTP 200).
- **[CMS QSO-25-18-CLIA (PDF)](https://www.cms.gov/files/document/qso-25-18-clia.pdf)** — the CMS memo with the blood, cells/tissue and organ applicability tables. Use it as the authority on which blood-center tests CLIA covers; it is policy guidance, not regulation. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-13 (HTTP 200; PDF, no HTML title).
- **[CMS: Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA)](https://www.cms.gov/medicare/quality/clinical-laboratory-improvement-amendments)** — the program overview and current notices. Re-check before relying on any date it carries. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-13 (HTTP 200).
- **[CMS: How to obtain a CLIA certificate (PDF)](https://www.cms.gov/regulations-and-guidance/legislation/clia/downloads/howobtaincliacertificate.pdf)** — a CMS general-information document on CLIA certification and certificate types. Read it for the plain-language version of the certificate types; confirm any fee or form detail against the CMS landing page above. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-13 (HTTP 200; PDF, no HTML title).
- **[CAP: Laboratory Accreditation Program](https://www.cap.org/laboratory-improvement/accreditation/laboratory-accreditation-program)** and **[CAP: Accreditation Checklists](https://www.cap.org/laboratory-improvement/accreditation/accreditation-checklists)** — CAP's own public description of deeming authority, two-year on-site peer inspections, 21 discipline checklists and custom checklists. These pages describe the checklists; they do not contain them. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-13 (HTTP 200 for both; titles "Laboratory Accreditation Program - CAP" and "Accreditation Checklists - CAP").
- **[2020 04 14 ACIL Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments CLIA Certification Process Webinar](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xUyNGY-VVX4)** (ACILmedia, from oEmbed `author_name`) — the video embedded in this lesson: a laboratory trade association's webinar on the CLIA certification process. Training content for independent labs, not CMS guidance and not blood-specific; dated 2020, so check current forms on CMS's page. Verified embeddable via YouTube oEmbed on 2026-11-13 (HTTP 200).

Earlier modules this lesson builds on: [Regulatory landscape orientation](../../../foundations/regulatory-landscape-orientation/index.qmd), [Collection and testing](../../blood-center-operations/collection-and-testing/index.qmd), [The AABB Assessment Process](../../fda-and-aabb-in-practice/the-aabb-assessment-process/index.qmd), [FDA Inspection Authority and Outcomes](../../fda-and-aabb-in-practice/fda-inspection-authority-and-outcomes/index.qmd).

## Keep learning

Not official sources, and not authority for any regulatory claim. Both articles are older than the sources above, so treat details as history and check them against the current CMS and CAP pages.

- **[QC for accreditation: CMS validation inspections](https://www.captodayonline.com/qc-accreditation-cms-validation-inspections/)** (CAP TODAY, from the 2015 issues) — how CMS re-inspects a sample of accredited labs to check the accreditor's work, which makes the "back door" in 493.61(b)(4) concrete. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-13 (HTTP 200).
- **[Top Laboratory Deficiencies Across Accreditation Agencies](https://myadlm.org/cln/articles/2018/july/top-laboratory-deficiencies-across-accreditation-agencies)** (Clinical Laboratory News, ADLM, 2018) — what accreditors most often cite, useful for sensing where inspectors spend time. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-13 (HTTP 200).
- **[CAP: Peer Inspections](https://www.cap.org/laboratory-improvement/accreditation/peer-inspections)** (CAP) — CAP's own page on its inspection model; this is the accreditor describing itself, so read it as program description. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-13 (HTTP 200; title "Peer Inspections - CAP").
